alternatives.argument: For the stated two normalized component densities and positive weights, direct summation gives m(1/4)=4/3. Dividing the two joint masses by this positive finite marginal gives responsibilities (1/2,1/2); substituting them into the complete-data log density gives the displayed Q formula.

The two-Bernoulli joint density sums to one; at current theta=1/2 the latent law is Bernoulli(1/2). Direct integration gives Q(theta|1/2)=0.5 log(theta^3(1-theta)); the exact factorization proves its unique maximizer is 3/4, while Q(7/10)-Q(1/2)=0.5 log(1029/625)>0 and the observed log-likelihood gain is log(7/5)>0.
